content.title: About
content.content: Coffee is a beverage made from roasted seeds of the coffee plant (genus Coffea). The main species are Arabica (Coffea arabica) and Robusta (Coffea canephora). Coffee has a distinctive aroma, a bitter‑acidic taste, and contains caffeine, a stimulant for the central nervous system.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Coffee is the second most traded commodity in the world after oil.
Arabica accounts for about 60‑70 % of global production, while Robusta makes up 30‑40 %.
The first commercial coffee was cultivated in Yemen in the 15th century.
There are over 100 Arabica varieties, each with its own flavor profile.
Coffee beans are not true beans; they are seeds inside the fruit called coffee cherries.

items.title: Energizing effect
items.content: Caffeine increases alertness, improves concentration, and can reduce feelings of fatigue.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Coffee is rich in polyphenols that help combat free radicals and may lower the risk of certain chronic diseases.

items.title: Metabolism support
items.content: Caffeine can boost metabolic rate, leading to a modest increase in calorie burning.

items.title: Reduced disease risk
items.content: Moderate coffee consumption is linked to lower risk of Parkinson’s disease, type‑2 diabetes, and some cancers.

items.title: Liver health
items.content: Regular moderate coffee intake may reduce the risk of cirrhosis and liver cancer.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience anxiety, insomnia, rapid heartbeat, or gastrointestinal upset after caffeine.

items.title: Blood pressure increase
items.content: High doses of caffeine can temporarily raise blood pressure, which is relevant for people with hypertension.

items.title: Mineral absorption
items.content: Caffeine can reduce the absorption of iron and calcium, so it’s advisable not to drink coffee immediately with these minerals.

items.title: Pregnancy
items.content: Pregnant women are advised to limit caffeine intake to about 200 mg per day (roughly one cup).

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Coffee is typically brewed with hot water (90‑96 °C) as espresso, drip, French press, or Turkish coffee. It can be enjoyed with milk, cream, sugar, spices (cinnamon, cardamom), or used in desserts, sauces, and marinades.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store whole beans in an airtight container in a cool, dark place, away from moisture and direct sunlight. For longer storage, keep them in the refrigerator or freezer, but avoid condensation when removing them.
